from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Flowing River", [
            "Vector fields assign direction to every point.",
            "Wind and water are natural examples.",
            "Points influence flow through expansion or rotation."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        stream = StreamLines(lambda p: np.array([0.5, 0.2*np.sin(p[0]), 0]), color="#2196F3")
        self.place_in_area(stream, "A1", "F6")
        
        velocity_label = Text("Flow Velocity", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(velocity_label, "E5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(stream), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#2196F3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        particles = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.03, color=WHITE) for _ in range(10)])
        for p in particles:
            p.move_to(stream.submobjects[np.random.randint(len(stream.submobjects))].point_from_proportion(np.random.rand()))
        self.add(particles)
        self.play(FadeIn(particles), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#4CAF50")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(velocity_label), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFC107")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Bridge: The Del Operator", [
            "Del is our mathematical tool.",
            "Divergence uses the dot product.",
            "Curl uses the cross product."
        ])
        
        # Define symbols (using tex_template if standard LaTeX environment issues arise, or ensuring valid syntax)
        del_op = MathTex(r"{\nabla}", color="#FFEB3B", font_size=72)
        div_op = MathTex(r"{\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F}}", color="#4CAF50", font_size=48)
        curl_op = MathTex(r"{\nabla \times \mathbf{F}}", color="#2196F3", font_size=48)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(del_op))
        self.place_at_grid(del_op, "B2")
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFEB3B"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(del_op))
        self.play(Write(div_op))
        self.place_at_grid(div_op, "B2")
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#4CAF50"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(div_op))
        self.play(Write(curl_op))
        self.place_at_grid(curl_op, "B2")
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2196F3"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Display all
        all_group = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"{\nabla}", color="#FFEB3B"),
            MathTex(r"{\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F}}", color="#4CAF50"),
            MathTex(r"{\nabla \times \mathbf{F}}", color="#2196F3")
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(all_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(all_group))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Visualizing Divergence and Curl in Vector Fields

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Flowing River
sections.content: Briefly define a Vector Field as a region where every point has an assigned magnitude and direction (e.g., wind or water flow). Introduce the two fundamental ways a point can 'influence' the flow around it: expanding/contracting (Divergence) or spinning (Curl).
sections.example: Imagine a flock of birds flying; the velocity vector at any point represents the bird's speed and direction.

sections.title: Divergence: The Source or Sink
sections.content: Define Divergence as the net flux out of an infinitesimal volume. Visually represent this as a 'fountain' (positive divergence) versus a 'drain' (negative divergence). If the fluid enters and leaves at the same rate, divergence is zero (incompressible flow).
sections.example: An expanding balloon (positive divergence) vs. a vacuum cleaner nozzle (negative divergence).

sections.title: Curl: The Micro-Rotation
sections.content: Define Curl as the tendency of a vector field to rotate a tiny paddlewheel placed at a point. If the paddlewheel spins counter-clockwise, the curl is positive; if clockwise, it is negative. It measures the 'twirliness' of the field.
sections.example: A rubber duck placed in a whirlpool: if the duck spins in place, the curl is non-zero at that point.

sections.title: Mathematical Bridge: The Del Operator
sections.content: Introduce the Del operator (∇) as the mathematical tool. Show Divergence as the dot product (∇ ⋅ F) and Curl as the cross product (∇ × F). Use a quick graphic showing how the dot product yields a scalar (amount of spread) and the cross product yields a vector (axis of rotation).
sections.example: Visualizing the ∇ operator as a 'Swiss Army Knife' of calculus that extracts different local properties.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Conclude with a summary table: Divergence tells us about local sources/sinks, while Curl tells us about local rotation. Reiterate that these are local measurements that define global flow behavior.
sections.example: A complex weather map: show regions of 'High Pressure' (divergence) and 'Cyclones' (curl) to solidify understanding.
